findings.title: CLAIMS.md's Blaster cross-check of the policy reads as covering every mint layout, but Blaster stops at five lines
findings.scenario: Take a minting context whose mint has six or more lines, for example the Seedelf line beside five other policies' tokens: a few hundred bytes, far under 16,384. The policy fails it. The kernel proves that (policy_accepts_iff through flatLine, and PolicyLinesAll at every length). No Blaster theorem covers it, though: PolicyLinesAnyTx, PolicyLinesFourAnyTx and PolicyLinesFiveAnyTx prove failure only for no lines and for 2 to 5 lines. Yet CLAIMS.md:7 says "Seedelf's are also proved by Blaster ... as a cross-check by another route", and CLAIMS.md:23 lists the policy's cross-checks as "PolicyPurposeAnyTx, PolicyRedeemerAnyTx, PolicyLines*AnyTx and Slice/'s Rule (by PolicyShapes)". PolicyShapes' family is `lineCount lines ≠ 1` at any count. So a reader takes the second route to cover every mint, when it covers none past five lines. The 128-signatory bound and the opaque slice are both disclosed in *Where it stops*; this bound isn't. README.md:120 adds "One property is proved in the kernel but not by Blaster". There are at least two more: mints of six lines or more, and the wallet past 128 signatories (README:93 explains that one by the size limit). README.md:202 also still points to "*By Blaster alone*", a section 1d41dfed renamed. The headline, kernel claim holds, and no money is involved: what's wider than its theorems is the extent of the secondary claim.
findings.since: 481ddb1f (CLAIMS.md: chunk 48's `LinesAll*` became `PolicyLines*AnyTx`); 1d41dfed (README's "One property" and the dangling *By Blaster alone*)
findings.evidence: seedelf-verification/Seedelf/PolicyShapes.lean:230-233: the third family is `(∀ l ∈ lines, l.2 ≠ []) ∧ lineCount lines ≠ 1 ∧ c = mintIn (... (mintOf lines)) (.B tag) own`. The Blaster theorems are PolicyLinesAnyTx.lean:102-122 (policy_fails_no_lines, _2, _11, _3, _12, _21, _111), PolicyLinesFourAnyTx.lean:88-111 (8) and PolicyLinesFiveAnyTx.lean:152-199 (16): 31 in all, the compositions of 2 to 5 lines plus none. The every-length results, policy_fails_two_or_more_lines (PolicyLinesAll.lean:81) and policy_fails_unless_one_line (LinesAllAnyMint.lean:123), are kernel. `git diff 363acdf3 HEAD -- seedelf-verification/CLAIMS.md` shows `-... PolicyRedeemerAnyTx, \`LinesAll*\` and Slice/'s Rule` changed to `+... PolicyRedeemerAnyTx, \`PolicyLines*AnyTx\` and Slice/'s Rule`. `git log -S 'One property is proved in the kernel but not by Blaster'` gives 1d41dfed. `git show 481ddb1f:seedelf-verification/README.md` has the heading `### By Blaster alone` at :116, which the current README renamed while keeping :202's reference to it.
findings.fix: In CLAIMS.md:23, put the kernel's every-length rows back beside the Blaster ones: "PolicyLines*AnyTx (no lines, and 2 to 5), PolicyLinesAll and LinesAllAnyMint (every length, the kernel)". Or add "(none and 2 to 5 lines)" the way "(none to 128 signatories)" is given. In README.md:118-121, name what has no Blaster route: the real slice, mints past five lines, and more than 128 signatories. Or reword "One property" to "One property the tools block". Point :202 at the renamed section. The same family: every list of the cross-checks, CLAIMS.md:7 and :23, README.md:29, :49 and :62, and PolicyShapes.lean:34's comment "(the PolicyLines…AnyTx modules)".

findings.title: README says the LinesAll kernel theorems list Lean's axioms alone, but nothing guards them, so a sorry there passes check.sh
findings.scenario: README.md:86 says the kernel-checked modules, "the LinesAll ones" among them, have a `#print axioms` that lists Lean's own alone. README.md:61 presents PolicyLinesAll and LinesAllAnyMint as kernel-checked at every length. But PolicyLinesAll.lean:173-177 and LinesAllAnyMint.lean:201-202 are bare `#print axioms`, with no `#guard_msgs`. No guarded theorem uses policy_fails_two_or_more_lines, policy_fails_unless_one_line or their _ctx forms: only flatten_apply_any reaches policy_accepts_iff, through PolicyRoot. Suppose a later edit leaves a `sorry`, `native_decide` or `blasterProven` in one of them, for example chunk 46's move onto PlutusCoreBlaster #77, which already reworks PolicyLinesAll's cek_rfl (chunk-46 plan :79, :95). `./check.sh seedelf-policy-any-tx` still prints `ok Seedelf.PolicyLinesAll`: check.sh fails a module only on lake's exit code or an Undetermined (check.sh:217-219), and README.md:197 says it doesn't fail one for a `sorry`. README:61 and :86 would then claim a kernel result the build no longer has. Nothing is false today: the cached build log (.lake trace, 2026-11-04) shows [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for all five PolicyLinesAll prints and both LinesAllAnyMint prints.
findings.evidence: `rg -n 'policy_fails_two_or_more_lines|policy_fails_unless_one_line|honest_one_line_returns_unit' -g '*.lean'` finds no uses outside PolicyLinesAll.lean and LinesAllAnyMint.lean. Seedelf/Every/PolicyRoot.lean:49 and :64 use only flatten_apply_any. The guarded modules are AnyTxShapes.lean:341-360, PolicyShapes.lean:268-291 and the seven CLAIMS cites. AnyTxCover.lean and PolicyAnyTx.lean print no axioms at all, but their rfl lemmas sit under guarded theorems (Typed.lean:146 and :181 use TxRest.ofTxInfo_infoWith and spendIn_of_spend; PolicyShapes uses mintIn_of_minting). Reading .lake/build/lib/lean/Seedelf/PolicyLinesAll.trace with python3 -I gives 5× 'depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]'.
findings.fix: Put `/-- info: ... -/ #guard_msgs in #print axioms` on the seven LinesAll theorems the README cites, as AnyTxShapes and PolicyShapes do. Alternatively, narrow README:86 to what is guarded: CLAIMS' citations, AnyTxShapes and PolicyShapes. The same family covers any README-cited kernel theorem outside a guard; AnyTx README's partial results only say "proves", so they're fine as worded.
findings.known_check: The audit's print-axioms-check (info) is closed by Audit.Checks.PrintAxioms. That covers the scenario modules only: its imports list no LinesAll module. Searched backlog.md, archive/plans/ and plans/ for "guard_msgs" and "print axioms": chunk 45 records guards on Lovejoin's top theorems, and chunk 46 notes #471's private blasterProven name. Nothing on LinesAll's missing guards.

findings.title: CLAIMS.md puts 'an input in every transaction' among Lovejoin's assumed ledger rules, but none of Lovejoin's theorems uses it
findings.scenario: CLAIMS.md:31 reads: "The ledger's rules, where they're used: in Lovejoin's kernel theorems, never in Seedelf's. The rules assumed are a value as the ledger forms it ..., a mint likewise ..., and an input in every transaction." None of Lovejoin's cited kernel theorems assumes an input. mix_logic_accepts_iff takes only hv, the reference inputs' validTxOutValue. one_shot_mint_accepts_iff takes hmint and houts. BoxPurposesAll.every_context_iff and reference_holder_every_context_errors take no hypothesis. The input rule belongs to the Seedelf policy's Blaster cover: PolicyShapes' policy_every_context_cover takes `hin : txInfoInputs ≠ []`, and policy_ledger_hypotheses derives it. So "never in Seedelf's" holds only for Seedelf's kernel theorems, while CLAIMS.md:23 names that cover in the same claim. It's a leftover. In the first CLAIMS.md (e6897cde) the policy's claim was Blaster's with that cover. Chunk 48 (04b57c4a) added "in Lovejoin's, never in Seedelf's" and kept the input rule. It claims an assumption nothing needs, so it says less, not more. It does point a reader at the wrong theorems.
findings.evidence: Readable.lean:224-226 (hv only); Readable.lean:257-261 (hmint, houts only); BoxPurposesAll.lean:64; PurposesKernel.lean:135; ReadableLaunch.lean:129-131 and ReadableOwner.lean:156-158 (no input hypothesis); PolicyShapes.lean:240-242 (`hin`) and :263-266. `git show e6897cde:seedelf-verification/CLAIMS.md` reads '- **The ledger's rules, where they're used.** Sorted values and maps, a well-formed mint, an input in every transaction.' `git show 04b57c4a -- seedelf-verification/CLAIMS.md` shows the change to '... in Lovejoin's, never in Seedelf's. ... and an input in every transaction.'
findings.fix: Say which theorem assumes which rule. mix_logic: the reference inputs' values. one_shot_mint: the mint and the outputs' values. mix_box and reference_holder: none. Seedelf's kernel theorems: none. Then say the policy's Blaster cover (PolicyShapes) assumes an input and a well-formed mint, or drop "an input in every transaction".
findings.known_check: Searched backlog.md, archive/plans/ and plans/ for "an input in every transaction" and "never in Seedelf": no hits. Searched Audit/review/findings.md (it predates CLAIMS.md): nothing.

guards.stops: Stops a Seedelf mint named after a first (smallest) input past #255. The policy refuses that mint (consByteString errors past a byte; policyAccepts' seedelfName = none), and its name's hex would come out misaligned.

mix_logic_of applies NFT_NAME "lovejoin", and one_shot_mint applies REFERENCE_HOLDER_HASH 288fea77 (:154). Every pool the wallet derives or verifies therefore sits on the parameters the kernel theorems are stated at (nftName, any P, any rh) and on the proved template bytes. A pool whose scripts aren't those isn't trusted.

checked_ok: All seven theorems in CLAIMS.md:13-21 exist under the stated full names: Seedelf.Every.wallet_accepts_iff, policy_accepts_iff and always_false_errors; Lovejoin.AnyTx.BoxPurposesAll.every_context_iff; Lovejoin.Every.Readable.mix_logic_accepts_iff and one_shot_mint_accepts_iff; Lovejoin.AnyTx.PurposesKernel.reference_holder_every_context_errors.

Each sits in a check.sh family. The Seedelf three are in seedelf-every (check.sh:58-63), the two Readable theorems in lovejoin-every (:183-188), and BoxPurposesAll and PurposesKernel in lovejoin-any-tx (:122, :148). All of these families are in README:170's standard command.

Each keeps `#guard_msgs in #print axioms` expecting [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]: Typed.lean:221, PolicyTyped.lean:234, AlwaysFalse.lean:33, Readable.lean:303/307, BoxPurposesAll.lean:106, PurposesKernel.lean:150. wallet_exec_iff and policy_exec_iff are covered through wallet_accepts_iff and policy_accepts_iff, which rewrite with them.

wallet_accepts_iff is stated over every typed V3 ScriptContext with no hypothesis: `∃ n, cekExecuteProgram wallet.script [toTerm ctx] n = Halt (VCon Unit) ↔ walletAccepts ctx`. walletAccepts matches README:41 clause by clause: spend only, the redeemer exactly Constr 0 [B,B,B], no datum or a non-Register datum accepts, and a Register needs schnorrProve with vkh ∈ the signatories, whatever the list.

policy_accepts_iff has no hypothesis, and policyAccepts matches README:42: a mint purpose, a B redeemer, flatLine exactly one line, a nonempty input list, seedelfName none past a byte (so a burn fails too), and the xor of burn and mint. sliceByteString is PlutusCoreBlaster's real def.
always_false_errors gives Error for some fuel and no Halt for any fuel, on any Data.

"Otherwise it reaches Error and never halts" (README:37) is backed by wallet_exec_error and policy_exec_error (guarded) and by exec_never_halts (LinesAllCek.lean:194, any program). cekExecuteProgram runs runStepsPreservingState, so an Error is never fuel running out.

mix_logic_accepts_iff holds at any P and at nftName = "lovejoin" (Template/Launch.lean:18), under one hypothesis: validTxOutValue on every reference input. That's exactly CLAIMS:31 and AnyTx README:46-48. The wallet derives mix_logic with NFT_NAME "lovejoin" (templates.rs:195), so every pool it verifies is in the theorem's scope.
one_shot_mint_accepts_iff holds at any seed, index and holder, under validMintValue and validTxOutValue on every output. launchOk matches AnyTx README:62-67.

CardanoLedgerApi's validTxOutValue (V1/Contexts.lean:808: ADA entry first with n > 0, policies and names strictly ascending, every quantity > 0) and validMintValue (V3/Contexts.lean:869: no ADA, nonzero, ascending) are what CLAIMS:31 paraphrases. The real ledger's V3 context meets both.
The _valid forms are narrower, as Readable.lean:15-19 and AnyTx README:72-76 say: V3 isBalanced (Contexts.lean:1209) has no deposit or withdrawal term. CLAIMS cites the forms that aren't _valid.

BoxPurposesAll.every_context_iff holds at any L with no hypothesis. The five other purposes error, and on a spend the first matching input's datum decides (datumPassesLedger: no datum or a hashed one passes, an inline box needs a ScriptCredential L withdrawal). That matches README:17 and AnyTx README:12-20.

reference_holder's proved bytes (Lovejoin/Scripts/reference_holder.hex) hash to 288fea77. That's the REFERENCE_HOLDER_HASH every v2 launch applies one_shot_mint with (templates.rs:72, :154), and lovejoin_proven_bytes_test.rs:35 asserts it.

toTerm P is `Const (Data (B P))` (CardanoLedgerApi IsData/Class.lean:56), so a template run with its parameters as arguments is the applied script's run, as apply_data and `aiken blueprint apply` build it. FlatDecodeCheck.lean:108-111 checks two such applications.
The default builtin semantics is variant E (PlutusCore Default/Basic.lean:55), as README:87 says.

At the pin, the BLS12-381 builtins, blake2b_224/256, byteStringToInteger (byteStringToIntegerOpaque), serialise_data (encodeDataOpaque) and xor (xorByteStringOpaque) are `opaque`, and sliceByteString is a def. That's what CLAIMS:30 and README:87 say.

The pins match README:132-140: lakefile and lake-manifest at 25c0ee0, 68c5399 and 9938562, and Slice/ at 96261cc. `git log 1c23de8..68c5399` in the fork shows the five changes named (opaque BSToInt, Fq1 as a Nat, BLS operand order, opaque serialise_data, opaque xor). The Lean-blaster fork is 46c8479 plus one fix and its test.

notes: A possible narrowing for the owner: CLAIMS.md:35's Not covered ("the classic pool's scripts") says less than the proofs give. FlatDecodeCheck.lean:110 guards that the classic pool's mix_box is mix_box's template applied at its L, so BoxPurposesAll.every_context_iff covers it. The classic reference_holder is the very file the cited theorem uses. Only the classic mix_logic, one_shot_mint and fee_contract are uncovered (the audit's classic-policy-fee-not-templates). The wording is conservative; narrowing it is the owner's call.

Where reference_holder's bytes come from isn't said. README:25 and CLAIMS:23 say Lovejoin's proofs are on "v2's templates, from Lovejoin's main at commit 29573c5". The reference holder is no template, and its proved bytes are the classic pool's c1239fb build. They are the same script every v2 launch names (288fea77), and the wasm test pins that, so the claim holds; one sentence saying where the holder's bytes come from would close the gap.
reference_holder_every_context_errors states only `∃ n, … = .Error`. "Never passes" (README:20) follows in one step from exec_never_halts, which no theorem spells out for the holder.

Two orphan modules, Lovejoin/AnyTx/LogicOwnerParserReach.lean and LogicOwnerPrefix.lean, are in no check.sh family and aren't imported by Lovejoin.lean, and nothing cites them. They will rot unbuilt (dead code).

Audit README:16 says the full evidence is in review/findings.json. That file holds 51 pre-merge rows split 1/10/13/20/7, against findings.md's merged 55 (1/8/13/24/8 plus 1 refuted). A reader comparing the two will find the counts disagree.

CLAIMS' trusted-base bullets name Lean's kernel, PlutusCoreBlaster's machine on a fork, CardanoLedgerApiBlaster's encoding, the opaque crypto and Z3 for Blaster. They don't say that the non-crypto builtins (consByteString, sliceByteString, equalsData, …) and the semantics variant (E) are also the model's; README:87 does. The ledger-rule hypotheses are CardanoLedgerApiBlaster's validTxOutValue and validMintValue, which CLAIMS paraphrases accurately but doesn't name.

No CI builds the proofs: .github/workflows has no Lean job, so the claims rest on the owner's own runs. The docs don't say when the last full run was. The cited modules haven't changed since 11-12, so this is a note, not a finding.
